validity.recommendation: no merge -- P6011 Project Maple is a separate, later Algonquin expansion proposal, not a revival/rescoping of Access Northeast
validity.researcher_notes: Tested the batch's lead that P6011 'Project Maple' re-scopes P0144 'Access Northeast'. Verdict: NO. Read Enbridge's own Project Maple Open Season Notice (infopost.enbridge.com, Sept-Nov 2023 open season, DocumentId ...1230040): Maple offers firm transportation from the Ramapo Receipt Point (west end, up to 500,000 Dth/d) and Salem Receipt Point (east end interconnect with Maritimes & Northeast, up to 250,000 Dth/d) -- together the roster's ~750 MMcf/d cap on P6011 -- with a target in-service as early as November 2029. That is a different scope (west/east receipt-point firm transport, no LNG storage), different receipt points (Ramapo/Salem vs. Access Northeast's Mahwah NJ/Ramapo NY/Brookfield CT supply + Rehoboth MA compressor + Acushnet/West Boylston MA M&R stations + new LNG facility), a different capacity (750 vs. 925 MMcf/d), and a different era (2023 open season vs. 2015-2017). They are both Algonquin-system expansions into New England but are not the same project. Separately: the EIA Aug-2026 release's row for a newer 2026 proposal 'Algonquin Project Beacon' (~300 MMcf/d, NY/CT/MA/RI, open season May-Jul 2026) notes 'Similar project (Maple) failed in 2023' -- i.e. Maple itself did not proceed and Beacon is Maple's successor, not Access Northeast's. Recommend the orchestrator route this Maple/Beacon lineage note to whichever agent works P6011.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1=Enbridge / Owner1%=100.00% is contradicted by TWO independent sources. CommonWealth Magazine (2017-06-29): 'The project is a joint initiative of Enbridge Gas Transmission and New England's two largest utilities, Eversource and National Grid.' offshore-technology.com/GlobalData: 'Developer Access Northeast, a joint venture (JV) of Eversource Energy, National Grid, Spectra Energy, and Spectra Energy Partners' (this predates the Feb-2017 Enbridge/Spectra merger -- Spectra Energy = pre-merger Enbridge). Both sources are consistent: Access Northeast was co-developed/financed by Enbridge(Spectra)+Eversource+National Grid, not solely owned by Enbridge. Neither source states exact equity percentages, so I cannot supply a corrected Owner1%/Owner2%/Owner3% -- leaving those blank rather than guessing (standing rule 2). Recommend adding Eversource Energy and National Grid as Owner2/Owner3 and researching the JV's actual equity split (likely in an Eversource or National Grid 10-K/8-K, not checked here) before asserting Enbridge=100%.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Recorded Status=cancelled is right and the cancellation itself is well-documented (June 2017 withdrawal from FERC pre-filing, citing 'gaps in legal authority' after Massachusetts's SJC struck down the ratepayer-funded pipeline-tax financing mechanism the project depended on -- see CommonWealth's related-article link on the SJC ruling). Checked whether the project was ever revived: no dated evidence found of a restart under the Access Northeast name; the batch's own lead (P6011 Project Maple) is a DIFFERENT, later Algonquin proposal, not a revival of this one (see validity[] duplicate-check note). No news newer than 2017 discusses 'Access Northeast' by name. Confirmed, not stale -- the evidence dates from the cancellation event itself, which is the correct anchor for a project that stopped existing in 2017 and was never revived under this name; the dormancy/staleness rules (2y/4y) apply to open questions about a still-pending project, not to a project independently confirmed dead and unrevived.
